concepts.title: Turning Tides: New Powers of the Age

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Turning Tides: New Powers of the Age' refers to.
questions.a: In the eleventh and twelfth centuries the tide of power turned: newer dynasties pressed old ones, trade caravans and fleets grew, and forces from beyond the north-west began to enter India.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Turning Tides: New Powers of the Age'.
questions.a: Centuries of settled kingdoms met new claimants, and India entered another age of readjustment.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Turning Tides: New Powers of the Age' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'The Cholas at Their Height' refers to.
questions.a: The Cholas of Thanjavur stood at their height: Rajaraja and Rajendra built a navy, sent expeditions across the seas, raised the Brihadishvara temple, and ran a rich administration of villages and temples.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Cholas at Their Height'.
questions.a: The Cholas showed what a sea-facing power could be: temple, fleet and village assembly working together.

questions.q: Under which section is 'The Cholas at Their Height' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Invasions from the North-West' refers to.
questions.a: From beyond the mountains came raiders: Mahmud of Ghazni repeatedly plundered the temples and towns of north-west India, and near the century's end Muhammad of Ghor's armies stayed to found a new sultanate.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Invasions from the North-West'.
questions.a: Wealth without united defence invited raids: India withstood the shocks, but the age changed its rulers and its maps.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Invasions from the North-West' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Caravans, Coasts and Trade' refers to.
questions.a: Caravans of traders crossed the passes and dusty roads, while ports on both coasts tied India to Southeast Asia and the Arab lands, moving textiles, spices, horses and ideas in every direction.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Caravans, Coasts and Trade'.
questions.a: Trade kept India rich and connected even in turbulent times: goods moved when armies could not.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Caravans, Coasts and Trade' taught, and from which source text?
